findings.title: Payload column is not valid CSV (double JSON.stringify)
findings.explanation: `JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(payload))` yields a JS string literal with backslash-escaped quotes, e.g. `"{\"a\":1}"`. CSV escapes a quote by doubling it (`""`), not with a backslash. Excel, Sheets and standard parsers will misparse or split these rows, and the payload is the main content of the export. Use a proper CSV escape helper (or a library such as `csv-stringify` or `fast-csv`): serialize the payload once with `JSON.stringify`, replace `"` with `""`, and wrap the result in quotes.

findings.title: `kind` and other fields are not escaped; CSV/formula injection possible
findings.explanation: `row.kind` is written raw. A comma, quote or newline in it corrupts the row structure. A value starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` can run as a formula when a customer opens the file in Excel or Sheets. If `kind` or any other column can contain user-influenced data, run every field through one escaping function. That function should quote the field, double embedded quotes, and prefix a `'` (or similar) to values starting with a formula character.

findings.title: No visible authorization or project-membership check
findings.explanation: The handler reads events for any `projectId` without checking that the caller may access that project. It exports up to 10,000 activity records, which may contain sensitive payloads. Confirm that router-level auth middleware verifies project membership. If the JSON events endpoint does this check inline or via a per-route middleware, reuse it here, and add a test that a user from another project or tenant gets 403 or 404. Also decide how archived projects should behave.

findings.title: `projectId` is not validated and errors are not handled
findings.explanation: `Number('abc')` is `NaN`, which makes Postgres throw. With Express 4, a rejected async handler is not forwarded to the error middleware, so the request can hang and trigger an unhandled rejection. Validate that `projectId` is a positive integer and return 400 otherwise. Wrap the handler in try/catch or an async wrapper that calls `next(err)`.

findings.title: Whole result set is buffered in memory; no streaming or backpressure
findings.explanation: Up to 10,000 rows, each with an unbounded JSON payload, are loaded into memory at once. Concurrent exports could add noticeable memory pressure. `res.write` return values are also ignored, so slow clients cause buffering. Consider streaming with a cursor (`pg-cursor` or `pg-query-stream`) and `pipeline`, and handle client disconnects. Also confirm that an index on `events (project_id, id)` exists so the `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT` query is cheap.

findings.title: Expensive endpoint has no rate limiting; response should not be cached
findings.explanation: Each request runs a 10k-row query and generates a large response, so it is an easy target for abuse. Apply rate limiting, or a stricter limit than the JSON endpoint. Add `Cache-Control: no-store` since the response contains private data.

findings.title: Silent truncation at 10,000 rows and duplicated query
findings.explanation: Customers asking for the 'activity log' may assume the file is complete. Document the cap, or signal truncation (for example an `X-Truncated` header or a UI note). The query and limit are also hard-coded and copied from the JSON endpoint. Extract a shared query function and a named constant, e.g. `EXPORT_LIMIT`, so the two do not drift apart.

findings.title: Assumes `created_at` is always a Date
findings.explanation: `row.created_at.toISOString()` throws if the column is nullable, or if the pg type parser returns strings. A throw mid-stream, after headers and part of the body have been sent, leaves a truncated file with a 200 status. Ensure the column is NOT NULL, or handle it defensively. Build the whole body, or validate the data, before writing the headers.

findings.title: Content-Type lacks charset; Excel may mangle UTF-8
findings.explanation: Use `text/csv; charset=utf-8`. Consider a UTF-8 BOM if customers open the file directly in Excel and payloads contain non-ASCII characters.

findings.title: Column order differs from the SELECT and the header is hand-maintained
findings.explanation: The SELECT order is `id, kind, payload, created_at` but the CSV order is `id, kind, created_at, payload`. Define the columns once and derive both the header and the row values from that list to avoid drift.

findings.title: No tests
findings.explanation: Add tests for CSV escaping (commas, quotes, newlines, formula prefixes, null payload), invalid `projectId`, the authorization failure case, and the 10,000-row cap.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Add CSV export for project events

Customers asked to download a project's activity log. Adds `GET /projects/:projectId/events.csv`, which returns the latest 10,000 events as CSV. Same query as the JSON events endpoint, larger limit.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/projects.ts b/src/routes/projects.ts
index c30f46c..b019274 100644
--- a/src/routes/projects.ts
+++ b/src/routes/projects.ts
@@ -49,3 +49,18 @@ projectsRouter.delete('/:projectId', async (req, res) => {
   await pool.query('UPDATE projects SET archived_at = now() WHERE id = $1', [projectId])
   res.status(204).end()
 })
+
+projectsRouter.get('/:projectId/events.csv', async (req, res) => {
+  const projectId = Number(req.params.projectId)
+  const { rows } = await pool.query(
+    'SELECT id, kind, payload, created_at FROM events WHERE project_id = $1 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10000',
+    [projectId],
+  )
+  res.setHeader('content-type', 'text/csv')
+  res.setHeader('content-disposition', `attachment; filename="project-${projectId}-events.csv"`)
+  res.write('id,kind,created_at,payload\n')
+  for (const row of rows) {
+    res.write([row.id, row.kind, row.created_at.toISOString(), JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(row.payload))].join(',') + '\n')
+  }
+  res.end()
+})
```

Report every problem you would raise in a code review, from blocking issues to nits. Respond with only a JSON object, no prose before or after it:

{"findings": [{"file": "path/to/file", "line": <line number in the new version, or null>, "severity": "blocking" | "non-blocking" | "nit", "title": "<short summary>", "explanation": "<why it matters and what to change>"}]}

Use an empty findings list if you would approve the pull request as it is. Write the review in English.
